title: Large Language Models
summary: How a decoder-only transformer turns your text into tokens, mixes them with causal self-attention, and picks the next token from a probability distribution, one token at a time.
objectives: **Trace** one forward pass of a decoder-only LLM from raw text to a sampled next token, naming the shape of the data at each stage
**Explain** in one sentence what self-attention outputs for a token (softmax(QKᵀ/√d_k) weights over earlier tokens, blending their **value** vectors) and why the causal mask uses -inf
**Predict** how temperature, top-k and top-p change the next-token distribution, using the logits [1.2, 0.9, 0.1, -0.5]
**Explain** why the KV cache is valid and what it costs (memory that grows linearly with sequence length)
**Distinguish** what attention does (mixes across positions) from what the FFN does (per position), and what changes at training vs inference time

steps.title: Autocomplete, but huge

state.caption: What comes next? Score every possible next piece

steps.narration: Your phone suggests the next word. A large language model does the same job at a huge scale: it reads all the text so far, gives a score to every possible next piece, picks one, adds it, and goes again [S1]. Every new piece means reading everything again from the start.

steps.title: Each word asks a question

state.caption: The newest word asks; earlier words answer

steps.narration: To make sense of the newest word, the model lets it ask a question, like a sticky note: *what am I sitting on?* Every word wears a folder label saying what it offers. Labels that match the note score higher [S9]. Here "on" and "sat" match best.
whatChanged: + sticky note on the newest word
+ a folder label on every word

steps.title: Take a blend, not one folder

state.caption: More from good matches, a little from the rest

steps.narration: The newest word doesn't open just one folder. It takes a mix of every folder's contents, more from the better matches, and becomes a richer version of itself [S9]. One rule: you may only open folders filed *before* you. Words that come later are locked [S3].

callout.text: Where the analogy breaks: it's a soft mix of *all* earlier folders, never just one.

whatChanged: + folder contents flow into the newest word

steps.title: The real names
steps.narration: Now the real names. The sticky note is the **query**, the folder label is the **key**, and the contents are the **value** [S9]. The only-earlier-folders rule is the **causal mask**. Each word's notebook, which every layer adds to, is the **residual stream** [S3]. This whole mixing step is **attention** [S4].

callout.text: Interview line: attention lets each token pull in information from earlier tokens, weighted by relevance.

steps.title: Text becomes tokens
steps.narration: First the text is cut into **tokens**: subword pieces from a fixed vocabulary. **BPE** builds that vocabulary by repeatedly merging the most frequent pair of symbols [S2]. GPT-2 uses byte-level BPE with **50,257** tokens, so any string can be encoded with no unknown token [S1]. Each token becomes an integer id.

steps.title: Ids become vectors
steps.narration: Each id picks one row of the **embedding matrix** E, shape [|V| × d]. Stack the five rows and you get **X**, shape [5 × d]: one d-dimensional vector per token [S3]. From here on, every layer reads and writes an [N × d] block like this one.
whatChanged: ~ ids used as row numbers into E

steps.title: Add position
steps.narration: Token embeddings carry no position, and attention by itself ignores order, so position must be injected [S3]. The original Transformer adds a sinusoidal vector to each row; learned position vectors worked about as well [S4]. Newer models such as LLaMA use **RoPE**, which rotates each query and key by an angle set by its position [S7][S8].

steps.title: Attention: score earlier tokens
steps.narration: Each token turns its vector into a **query**, a **key** and a **value** [S3]. The last token's query is dotted with every key, giving one row of scores; all rows together form QKᵀ, shape [5 × 5] [S4]. Scores are divided by √d_k, and cells above the diagonal, the future, become **-inf** [S3].

callout.text: Training uses the same mask: every position predicts its own next token in one pass, with the true previous tokens as input (teacher forcing) [S3].

steps.title: Attention: blend the values
steps.narration: Softmax turns the row into **weights** that sum to 1. The output is the weighted sum of the **value** vectors: a new vector for "the" that now carries context, mostly from "on" and "sat" [S4][S3]. This is the step people forget: attention outputs a blend of values, not a choice of one word.

callout.text: Interview line: attention output = softmax(QKᵀ/√d_k)·V, a relevance-weighted blend of earlier tokens' values [S4].

steps.title: Many heads, then the FFN, then repeat
steps.narration: Attention runs in **h heads** at once, each on a d/h slice; their outputs are concatenated and projected [S4]. Then a **feed-forward network** processes each position on its own [S3]. Both add their result into the **residual stream**, and the block repeats L times; LLaMA-7B has 32 layers, 32 heads, d = 4,096 [S8].

callout.text: Only attention moves information between positions; the FFN never looks at other tokens [S3].

whatChanged: ~ both add into the residual stream

steps.title: One score per vocab token
steps.narration: After the last block, only the last position's vector **h**, shape [1 × d], predicts the next token [S3]. Multiplying by Eᵀ gives one **logit** per vocabulary token, shape [1 × |V|]; softmax turns the logits into a **probability distribution** [S3]. The model outputs a distribution, not a word.

callout.text: No weights change at inference: generating text is a forward pass only [S3].

steps.title: Pick, append, repeat
steps.narration: A **decoding rule** picks one token from the distribution, here "mat" [S5]. It is appended and the model runs again; that loop is all generation is [S9]. The **KV cache** keeps every layer's past keys and values, so each new step computes q, k and v for the new token only [S6].
whatChanged: + one K and one V card per layer
~ q is used once, not stored

steps.title: Edge case: the window fills
steps.narration: The **context window** is a hard limit: GPT-2 takes at most 1,024 tokens [S1]. Meanwhile the KV cache gains one entry per token in every layer, so its memory grows linearly with length [S6]. Long chats and documents cost memory even though each step's compute stays manageable.

code.title: One decode step (pseudocode)
code.src:
def decode_step(x_new, cache, tau=1.0, top_p=0.9):
    h = embed(x_new) + pos(len(cache))          # [1 x d]
    for layer in layers:
        a = layer.norm1(h)
        q, k, v = a @ Wq, a @ Wk, a @ Wv        # new token only
        cache[layer].append(k, v)               # KV cache
        K, V = cache[layer].keys, cache[layer].values
        w = softmax(q @ K.T / sqrt(d_k))        # past + self only
        h = h + (w @ V) @ Wo                    # residual add
        h = h + ffn(layer.norm2(h))             # position-wise
    logits = final_norm(h) @ E.T                # [1 x |V|]
    p = softmax(logits / tau)                   # temperature
    p = keep_nucleus(p, top_p)                  # top-p, renormalise
    return sample(p)

steps.title: Attention, exactly
steps.narration: Each token's vector is projected three ways: q_i = x_iW^Q, k_j = x_jW^K, v_j = x_jW^V [S3]. Then Attention(Q,K,V) = softmax(QKᵀ/√d_k)V [S4]. Row i of the weights says how much of each value v_j flows into token i's output. In this example, row "the" puts 0.38 on "on" and 0.28 on "sat".

callout.text: The pseudocode leaves out the split into heads to stay short; step 3 adds it.

steps.title: Why √d_k and why -inf
steps.narration: If q and k have independent unit-variance entries, q·k has variance d_k, so large d_k pushes softmax into regions with tiny gradients [S4]. Dividing by √d_k keeps scores in range. Masked cells get **-inf** because e^-inf = 0; a score of 0 would still earn weight e^0 = 1 [S3].
whatChanged: - unscaled: one weight ≈ 0.92, the rest starve

steps.title: Heads and sizes
steps.narration: The base Transformer has d_model = 512 and h = 8 heads, so d_k = 64; MultiHead = Concat(head₁…head_h)W^O [S4]. LLaMA-7B uses d = 4,096, 32 heads and 32 layers [S8]. The FFN is position-wise with d_ff ≈ 4d; SwiGLU versions use about ⅔ of that [S3][S8].

steps.title: Logits to probabilities
steps.narration: The LM head computes logits u = hEᵀ, shape [1 × |V|], then y = softmax(u) [S3]. For logits [1.2, 0.9, 0.1, -0.5] the top token gets **0.44** [S3]. In training, the loss at each position is -log p(true next token), with the true earlier tokens as input: **teacher forcing** [S3].

steps.title: Temperature reshapes the distribution
steps.narration: Temperature divides the logits before softmax: softmax(u/τ) [S3]. At τ = 0.5 the top token rises to **0.59**; at τ = 0.1, **0.95**; at τ = 100 all four sit near **0.25** [S3]. As τ → 0 it becomes greedy decoding [S5]. Temperature changes the probabilities themselves, not what the model knows.

callout.text: Myth: temperature only changes the sampling step. It rescales the logits, so the probabilities themselves change [S3].

steps.title: Top-k vs top-p
steps.narration: **Top-k** keeps the k most likely tokens, however much probability they hold [S3]. **Top-p** keeps the smallest set whose cumulative probability reaches p, so its size adapts: in Hugging Face's example, p = 0.92 kept 9 tokens in one case and 3 in another [S5][S12]. Both renormalise what they keep, then sample.

steps.title: KV cache: what and why
steps.narration: Each layer caches past keys and values, shape [batch, heads, seq_len, head_dim] [S6]. That is valid because the causal mask means past k and v never change. Per-step attention cost drops from quadratic to linear, but memory grows linearly with length [S6]. **GQA** lets groups of query heads share KV heads, shrinking the cache [S10].

callout.text: KV memory per token ∝ 2 × layers × KV heads × head_dim, read straight off the cache shape [S6].

whatChanged: + one K and V per layer per token

steps.title: "Temperature 0 is deterministic"?
steps.narration: Greedy decoding is deterministic on paper. In practice, servers batch requests together, and many GPU kernels give slightly different numbers at different batch sizes [S11]. One test ran 1,000 completions at τ = 0 and got **80** unique outputs; with batch-invariant kernels it got **1** [S11].

quiz.q: Logits [1.2, 0.9, 0.1, -0.5] give the top token p = 0.44 at τ = 1. What is it at τ = 0.5?
quiz.why: Dividing logits by τ < 1 sharpens the softmax: 0.59 at τ 0.5 and 0.95 at τ 0.1 [S3].

quiz.q: For one token, what does a self-attention head output?
options: The single most relevant earlier token's vector
A weighted sum of value vectors from itself and earlier tokens
The full N × N attention score matrix for the sequence
The plain average of every token embedding in the prompt
quiz.why: softmax(QKᵀ/√d_k) weights blend the value vectors into a new vector; the mask limits it to itself and earlier positions [S4][S3].

quiz.q: Which decoding method changes how many candidate tokens it keeps, based on the model's confidence?
quiz.why: Top-p keeps the smallest set whose cumulative probability reaches p, so its size adapts [S5][S12].

quiz.q: X is [N × d] and the vocabulary has |V| tokens. What shape are the logits used to predict the next token?
quiz.why: The last position's [1 × d] vector times Eᵀ [d × |V|] gives [1 × |V|] [S3].

quiz.q: Which component moves information between token positions?
quiz.why: The FFN is position-wise; attention is the only part that mixes information across positions [S3].

quiz.q: While generating, which tokens can the 4th token in the sequence attend to?
quiz.why: The causal mask sets scores for j > i to -inf, leaving the token itself and earlier tokens [S3].

quiz.q: d_model = 512 with 8 heads. What is d_k per head?
quiz.why: d_k = d_model / h = 64 in the base Transformer [S4].

quiz.q: What happens to the model's weights while it answers your prompt?
options: They stay fixed; it only conditions on context
They update slightly toward your prompt
The KV cache rewrites the FFN weights
quiz.why: Generation is a forward pass; weights change only in training, via the cross-entropy loss [S3].
